For the bedrooms, identify wardrobe dimensions, loft requirements, bed or headboard work and any study or dressing units. Prepare a base scope around the client s agreed priorities. Keep accessories, decorative ceilings, premium hardware and additional storage as clearly priced options when they have not yet been selected. Show the amount added or replaced by an option so the client can make a meaningful decision.

With quantity in E2 and rate in F2, the line amount in G2 can be =ROUND(E2*F2,2). Copy the formula through the item rows and use =SUM(G2:G20) for a schedule ending at row 20. Adjust that range to the actual schedule; adding rows outside a fixed range can leave work out of the total.

Separate base units, wall units, tall units and lofts where their specifications or measurement methods differ. For every conversion, keep the original measurement available. Rounding each small component too early can create a different result from rounding the final item quantity.

Visually distinguish input cells from formula cells, and protect formula ranges against accidental edits where appropriate. Keep a clean template without previous client details. Consider a cabinet measured on its front elevation: 8 ft × 7 ft = 56 sq ft. The rate must use that same square-foot basis. The figures below demonstrate spreadsheet arithmetic only; they are not a market rate or a project estimate.

Unit cell D2: sq ft. Quantity E2: 56. Illustrative rate F2: 100. Formula G2: =ROUND(E2*F2,2). Calculated amount: 5,600. If the verified quantity changes to 60, the amount becomes 6,000 without retyping the total.

It starts with a conversation: a family wants a more useful kitchen, an office needs a new layout, or a homeowner has a budget but no agreed scope. Before you can price the work, you need to understand the client, the property and the decisions still to be made.

When that context sits in one spreadsheet and the quotation sits somewhere else, small changes become difficult to explain. A revised finish may change the rate. A site measurement may change the quantity. A client may accept the kitchen while asking you to postpone the wardrobes. The useful question is not simply whether you have a CRM. It is whether the next person can understand which client, scope and proposal they are looking at.

Be specific about what the client has asked for. ‘Kitchen interiors’ could mean base units only, a full modular kitchen or cabinetry plus electrical changes and civil work.
